label: Icon system asset
description: A single icon or a coherent icon family member.
instructions: Begin with the semantic job and choose one instantly readable metaphor.
Use the specified grid, stroke, corner and optical correction rules; do not imitate the logo literally unless requested.
Describe vector construction, bounding box, padding, alignment, colour states, small-size behaviour and accessibility.
If an image engine is used, request a clean isolated symbol with no mockup, words, letters, watermark or background scene.
productionChecklist: Meaning is understandable without a label
Silhouette remains clear at the minimum target size
Stroke weights and corner treatment match the family
Filled, outline, active and disabled states use approved colours
No accidental logo, letter or culturally ambiguous symbol
SVG geometry can be reconstructed from the result
outputContract: Construction specification with grid, stroke, padding and colours

label: Logo or brand signature
description: A logo refinement, lockup or approved variant.
instructions: Express a durable brand idea, not a current campaign slogan.
Specify symbol, wordmark, lockup geometry, clearspace, scale limits, monochrome behaviour and background variants.
Reject generic AI-logo tropes, gradients without semantic purpose and effects that fail in one colour.
productionChecklist: Recognisable in monochrome
Legible at minimum size
Distinct from common category marks
Clearspace and lockups documented
Asset and trademark questions resolved
Vector master required
outputContract: Misuse list and legal review notes

label: LinkedIn post
description: A brand-correct organic LinkedIn post and optional visual direction.
instructions: Choose one concrete tension, observation or piece of proof and build the post around it.
Write for the named audience and the channel's reading rhythm; do not convert the post into a brochure.
Use a specific opening, short paragraphs, one coherent argument and the approved CTA hierarchy.
If a visual accompanies the post, give a separate art-direction brief without placing paragraphs of text inside the image.
productionChecklist: Opening earns attention without ragebait unless the brand allows it
One claim per paragraph
Every factual claim is evidenced
Voice matches locale and register
No generic LinkedIn cadence or inflated conclusion
CTA is proportionate to the post
outputContract: Short compliance note with unresolved facts

label: Brand photograph
description: A photorealistic brand image or a coherent photographic series.
instructions: Define the image's communication job before specifying people, place or camera.
Describe people only through an explicit representation policy or the task brief; never infer sensitive attributes from names, faces or industry stereotypes.

Specify subject count, age range, presentation, roles, behaviour, wardrobe, environment, moment, composition, camera height, lens character, depth of field, light direction, colour temperature, palette, surface texture, grade and crop-safe space.
Demand lived-in physical detail and believable work; reject stock-photo gestures, plastic skin, fake text, fake logos and impossible hands or tools.
productionChecklist: People and casting follow explicit policy
Scene shows a credible moment rather than a pose
Camera, lens and light produce the intended emotion
Brand palette appears through environment and grade, not coloured fog
Crop works at requested aspect ratio
No text, logo, watermark or invented certification
Consent and privacy requirements are satisfied

label: Photo graphic
description: A photograph combined with graphic composition for social, editorial or campaign use.
instructions: Separate raster generation from typography and layout: generate a clean photograph first, then compose real text with the approved type system.
Reserve explicit negative space for headline and CTA; specify hierarchy, grid, crop variants and safe areas.
Keep overlays and effects tied to the visual concept rather than decoration.
productionChecklist: Photograph works without generated text
Headline remains live typography
Grid, type, colour and spacing are brand-correct
Desktop and mobile crops preserve the subject
Contrast passes
Claims and CTA are evidenced

label: Brand video
description: A short film, social video, product film or motion graphic.
instructions: Build a time-based argument with a specific beginning, turn and ending.
Specify shot intent, action, framing, camera movement, duration, transition logic, sound, music, voiceover and on-screen typography for every beat.
Keep human performance natural and product behaviour physically plausible.
Provide captions, audio-description considerations and reduced-motion alternatives.
productionChecklist: Every shot advances the message
Casting follows policy
Motion grammar is consistent
Music and sound support rather than mask speech
Captions and safe-area typography are planned
No invented product behaviour or claims
End frame and CTA match the channel
outputContract: Shot list with camera and action

label: Brochure or document
description: A printed or PDF brochure, dossier, report or sales document.
instructions: Define reader, decision and page journey before writing copy.
Specify cover, navigation, section rhythm, proof placement, callouts, charts, image crops, paper/PDF behaviour, margins, bleed and accessibility.
Use real typography for all text and keep generated images free of words and logos.
productionChecklist: Document has one reader and decision
Page order supports scanning and deep reading
Facts and sources are visible
Type remains legible in print and PDF
Images are high enough resolution
Bleed, safe area and export profile are defined
Tagged-PDF or accessible digital alternative is planned

label: Advertisement
description: A paid static, carousel, display or social advertisement.
instructions: Select one audience, one tension, one offer and one action per concept.
Distinguish a creative hypothesis from a verified claim and label required substantiation.
Design the first-frame or static image to communicate before the body copy is read.
Return production variants without weakening the core brand idea.
productionChecklist: One audience and action
Hook matches landing destination
Claim is substantiated
Logo and CTA remain legible at placement size
Visual is recognisable without clickbait
Platform text and safe-area limits are met
Variant differences are testable

label: Website design and copy
description: A complete website, landing page or reusable web component.
instructions: Map visitor intent, information architecture, proof and conversion before styling components.
Translate brand rules into semantic design tokens, responsive layout, interaction states and reusable components.
Use verified source content and expose open questions instead of filling gaps with generic copy.
productionChecklist: Offer understood in five seconds
Information hierarchy follows audience questions
Every component uses shared tokens
Mobile interaction is equivalent to desktop
WCAG checks pass
No horizontal overflow at 390 px
Performance, SEO and structured data are tested
Claims and legal content remain exact

label: Presentation
description: A pitch, keynote, internal deck or client presentation.
instructions: Build the spoken argument first; slides are visual support, not a document pasted onto frames.
Define opener, tension, proof sequence, turning point and close.
Specify master layouts, type sizes, chart rules, image crops and speaker-note expectations.
productionChecklist: One idea per slide
Narrative works aloud
Type is legible from the back of a room
Proof and sources are visible
Charts use approved semantic colours
Images follow casting policy
Deck has a clear next action
